Sub: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation: Ornab] over Westcentral Bay of
Bengal close to Andhra Pradesh coast [Post Landfall Outlook for Andhra Pradesh and
adjoining South Odisha coasts—Red Message]
The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation :Ornab] over Westcentral Bay of Bengal off Andhra
Pradesh coast remains practically stationary during past 03 hours, and lay centered at 0530 hrs IST of
today, the 28th October, 2026 over the, near latitude 16.4°N and longitude 82.0°E, about 30 km east of
Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 45 km south-southwest of Yanam (Puducherry UT), 70 km south-southwest
of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 90 km east-northeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), and 170 km
east-northeast of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).
It is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and
Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained
wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph during next 2 hours.
Very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” is continuing to interact with the land surface and Wall cloud region
of northern sector has further entered into the land. Centre of the system is very close to the coast line
and the landfall process will continue during next 2 hours.
The system is under continuous surveillance of the Doppler Weather Radar at Machilipatnam.
Forecast location and intensity are given in following table:
